 ---- Respondent 20/07/2023

Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 08.02.2023 passed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge FTSC (POCSO Act), Baloda Bazar,
CG in Special Criminal Case (POCSO) No. 73/2021, the appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 363,366 and 376 IPC and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 5 years on each count u/Ss. 363,366 & 376 IPC with fine of Rs. 500/- with default stipulation and to undergo RI for 20 years with fine of Rs. 1000/-
with default stipulation u/s. 6 of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text: Heard Mr. Pushpendra Kumar Patel, counsel for the appellant and Mr. Wasim Miyan, Panel Lawyer for the State on the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (I.A. No. 01).

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the victim is aged about 17 years and 3 months and it appears that it is a case of elopement and not of taking away and enticing away and as per the statement recorded by the victim/girl (PW-1) it transpires that she has voluntarily eloped with the appellant and he has been staying with him in his house.

It is argued that the present FIR appears to have been lodged against the appellant only on the fact that the parents of the victim/girl were against the relationship of the victim with the appellant and in the medical report though allegation of rape has been alleged but the same does not corroborate with the statement of the victim.

He further argued that the appellant is in jail since 01.09.2021 and further the fact that the appeal is likely to take a couple of years or even more in its final disposal, hence he prays that the appellant be enlarged on bail.
Notice has been served on the objector but none appeared.
Mr. Wasim Miyan, learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the State/respondent formally opposes the prayer for grant of bail.
We have heard counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended with the bail application.

sentences.text: Taking into account that it is a case of love relation between the appellant and the victim and she appears to have eloped voluntarily with him.

As per the statement of victim (PW-2), she has stated that she independently eloped with the appellant and is staying with him in his house and the medical report though allegation of rape has been levelled but the same does not corroborate with the statement of the victim.

Thus, taking into consideration the fact that the appellant is in jail since 01.09.2021 and that the further hearing of this appeal would take prolonged period of time, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to the appellant by the learned trial court is hereby suspended.

He shall be released on his executing a bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 07.08.2023.

They shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, I.A. No. 01 is allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only confined for disposal of aforesaid I.A. filed in this appeal and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the matter.
List this case for final hearing.
C.c. as per rules.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal) (Ramesh Sinha)
